gateway.principalUse: audit projection only on current execution owner path

consequence: When Gateway-to-Runtime owner bearer routing is restored under the observed static Runtime configuration, distinct authenticated Gateway users collapse to one Runtime service principal.
Runtime principal-scoped admission/idempotency/credential mechanisms therefore cannot express end-user isolation through this Gateway composition.
Job lifecycle and Artifact access through owner object identifiers are not scoped by an EffectivePrincipal in the deployed MCP handlers.
Gateway audit can retain the end-user principal while Runtime Job truth records a service principal, creating a cross-layer attribution split.
acceptance: Preserve a factorized authenticated subject across Gateway-to-Runtime, or enforce Security authorization at Gateway with explicit subject/action/resource decisions before owner calls.
Add object-level authorization to Job/Artifact lifecycle actions.
Keep Gateway service identity distinct from delegated end-user identity.
Add two-principal negative tests proving principal A cannot resolve/get/observe/cancel/read principal B's operation or artifacts.
nonClaims: AF-S2 was already documented OPEN before this campaign and is not double-counted as a new gap.
Gateway Runtime carriers were unavailable during the observation, so no cross-user live cancel/read exploit was executed.
ActorRef/Social Work identity semantics are outside this evidence object.
